title: decode.rs: QP false-truncation guard has three-level nesting that is hard to reason about
description: mime-tree/src/decode.rs: the QP decode-limited path has three nested levels of logic — (1) the input limiting and input_was_limited flag, (2) the check for whether output bytes were actually cut, and (3) the fallback full decode. The interaction between these levels is subtle: the guard fires only when input was limited AND decoded output <= n, meaning the decoder stopped exactly at the limit with no left-over. Extracting this into a named helper (fn qp_with_limit(input, n) -> (Vec<u8>, bool)) with a clear contract in its doc comment would make the three-level interaction a local decision inside one function rather than inlined control flow.
